seo_title: Mothercare SG Case Study: Reaching New Mothers | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read 4,049 posts and ads from 11 baby and parenting brands for Mothercare SG and found new mothers the most addressed type, identified 2,999 times.
eyebrow: Brand case study · Baby and maternity retail · Singapore
h1: Mothercare SG should inspire new mothers, then convert within their budget
lede: For Mothercare SG, SOMIN read 4,049 Instagram, Facebook and Ads Library items from 11 baby and parenting brands, including Mummys Market, Babyland and Hatchery Cribs. New mothers were the most addressed type of mother, identified 2,999 times, so SOMIN mapped the personas and tensions brands use to reach them in ads and in organic posts.
meta_line: A SOMIN custom study · Singapore · New mothers

challenge.title: New mothers face a lifestyle shock and a financial concern
challenge.body: New mothers are the most addressed type of mother in the category's content, but they are not one audience. Having a child, especially for the first time, is a lifestyle shock, and it is always a financial concern. The study asked how brands speak to new mothers in ads versus organic posts, and which challenges they address.

approach.title: 4,049 items sorted by mother type, persona and tension
points: Collected Instagram, Facebook and Ads Library content from 11 brands, including MothercareSG, Mummys Market, Babyland, Kiddy Palace and Pupsik: 4,049 items.
Classified every item by the type of mother it addressed, from expectant mothers to empty nesters, and isolated the content aimed at new mothers.
Detected the personas and tensions in new-mother content, split by ads and organic posts, and compared total media, total engagement and post-to-engagement ratios.
Added psychological, sociological and economic reasons behind the tensions as starting points for communication angles.

findings_title: How 11 baby brands address new mothers in ads and posts

findings.title: Ads sell savings, posts sell family life
findings.body: In ads, the Family-Centered Savings Seeker dominated with 131 items. In organic posts, the Family-Centered Wellness Advocate led with 2,416 items and 80,573 engagements.

findings.title: Affordable quality dominates both channels
findings.body: Affordable and High-Quality Baby Products was the top tension in ads, with 90 items, and in posts, with 1,120 items.

findings.title: Life beyond the product engages more
findings.body: Creating Safe and Comfortable Spaces for Babies drew the most post engagement, 39,657 from 797 posts, and the analyst found parenthood challenges more socially engaging than affordable, high-quality baby items.

delivered.title: Mothercare SG's new-mother map of personas and tensions
points: A breakdown of the types of mother addressed, led by new mothers (2,999), mothers of infants (2,308) and mothers of toddlers (1,823)
5 ad personas and 4 post personas, each sized by media and engagement
5 ad tensions and 5 post tensions that brands address for new mothers
Psychological, sociological and economic reasons behind the tensions, to inspire creative directions

quote.text: When it comes to purchasing, it’s about providing the best you can within your budget.

outcome.title: Mothercare SG needs a funnel from aspiration to budget
outcome.body: Proper funnelling is essential. In awareness and consideration, tapping into an aspirational mindset is very powerful; at the bottom of the funnel, the focus should be on how Mothercare SG can help fulfil those aspirations within a mother's financial means. That calls for different activities and a clear purpose for each platform.

faq.q: Which brands were in the study?
faq.a: Baby Kingdom, Babyland, Cotton On Kids, First Few Years, Hatchery Cribs, Kiddy Palace, MothercareSG, Motherswork, Mummys Market, Pramfox and Pupsik.

faq.q: How do ads and posts differ when they talk to new mothers?
faq.a: Ads lean on savers and value seekers, such as the Family-Centered Savings Seeker. Posts lean on family-centric wellness advocates, and other personas also earn higher engagement ratios, which shows the new mother persona is multi-faceted.

faq.q: Are the reasons behind the tensions based on market data?
faq.a: No. They are textbook psychological, sociological and economic theories, offered to inspire creative directions. SOMIN typically cross-references them with other sources, such as survey or BI data, to verify relevance.
